task:
Implement the remaining functional Phase 12 scope on the existing branch feat/phase-12-android-companion at commit 3b7c00e (real Android APK/client already present). Use the absolute checkout-local toolchain paths from prior requests and leave `.tooling/` untracked. Read the roadmap Phase 12/13 sections, current companion.rs/gateway.rs/lib.rs/contracts/UI, Android client/protocol, migrations, docs, and AGENTS.md before editing.

Implement an actual desktop companion transport, not metadata: add a focused Rust module (for example companion_transport.rs) with a bounded std::net TCP listener and per-connection lifecycle. It must be disabled by default and start only through an explicit Owner-confirmed Tauri command; bind 127.0.0.1 by default and allow only explicitly confirmed RFC1918/private binding, never 0.0.0.0/public. Use a versioned `aip-companion-v1` newline-delimited bounded JSON envelope matching the Android client, strict maximum frame/field/payload lengths, protocol negotiation, one-time in-memory pairing code/fingerprint exchange, HMAC-SHA-256 challenge-response, per-session nonce and monotonically increasing replay counter, constant-time MAC verification, timeouts, typed errors, idempotency, reconnect, key rotation and revocation, clean stop/connection shutdown, and no raw secret/payload logging or SQLite raw-secret persistence. Keep only ephemeral secrets in a synchronized runtime state; use existing Rust/SQLite Owner/agent/safe-mode/temporary-chat/quota/audit authority for every history/queue operation. Do not expose Python internals, create a relay, telemetry, watcher, or public listener.

Expose bounded Tauri commands and typed contracts/UI for transport status/start/stop and one-time pairing metadata, with explicit Portuguese warnings and private-binding confirmation. Integrate the Android Kotlin client with a real Socket/SocketTimeout transport against this protocol (offline fallback remains truthful), securely load the Keystore pairing secret, perform handshake/version/auth/replay checks, and support bounded read-only history plus preview/approve/cancel/retry queue requests. Add deterministic Rust loopback integration tests using an ephemeral local port and a real std::net client, plus Android JVM protocol/socket tests for handshake, HMAC, replay, disconnect/reconnect, bounds, revocation, and offline fallback. Keep existing synthetic companion/gateway fixture paths intact. Add the minimum migration only if durable audit metadata is required; never persist raw credentials/media.

Add `.tooling/`, `android/.gradle/`, `android/app/build/`, and equivalent generated Android outputs to .gitignore so secrets scan/status are not flooded by the untracked local toolchain. Update docs/PHASE_12_ANDROID_IMPLEMENTATION.md, docs/PHASE_12_ANDROID_SPEC.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md, docs/CORRECTIVE_GAP_MATRIX.md, README.md, and any contracts/UI status text truthfully: Phase 12 real APK + authenticated local/private transport/loopback is functional; physical-device UX, network/private-LAN smoke, and release signing remain human/release checks; Phase 13 BielOS/Cloudflare integration remains AIP-side metadata/contract work only.

Run and report: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked --lib plus focused transport/companion tests; contracts typecheck/build/tests; desktop typecheck/tests/build; Android `gradle.bat --no-daemon testDebugUnitTest lintDebug assembleDebug`; APK SHA-256; `pnpm secrets:scan`; `git diff --check`; clean Git status excluding ignored toolchain/build output. Commit only this transport/integration scope with exact message `feat: add phase 12 authenticated companion transport`. Do not push, publish, PR, merge, tag, release, deploy, modify BielOS, use native subagents, or edit directly outside the configured Biel4 Executor.

If any requirement cannot be implemented securely, stop with a precise blocker rather than claiming a fake network success.
constraints: Use only the configured Biel4 App Server Executor in fast mode; no native subagents or alternate backend.
Use absolute checkout-local toolchain paths; leave .tooling untracked and never commit it.
Transport must be real, authenticated, bounded, explicit, local/private-only by default, and fail-closed; no relay/public listener/telemetry/raw secret/media.
Preserve existing fixture companion/gateway commands and Rust/SQLite Owner/agent/safe-mode/temporary-chat/idempotency/audit gates.
Do not import BielOS code or implement external Phase 13 integration.
